title: Superflow vs Ruttl
kicker: · SUPERFLOW VS RUTTL · THE AI QA REVIEWER FOR AGENCIES
headline: Ruttl is a feedback tool. Superflow is a feedback tool + a team.
secondary: The team is AI agents, built from your QA checklist. They check every site change and pin what they find. Your team decides. Your client approves from a link.
prevents: Stop finding every mistake by hand.
No more manual pass before launch.
qualifier: If your agency reviews client sites in Ruttl, this page is for you.
heroCaption: It's like Ruttl hired a QA team.

dimensions.label: Who checks the site
dimensions.framing: Ruttl was built before AI could check a site.
leftFacts: Agents run your checklist. Every change, desktop and mobile.
Findings land as pinned comments, rationale attached.
rightFacts: A person checks it. Nothing scans the site for mistakes on its own.
Ruttl AI is scoped to comment sentiment analysis and site performance suggestions. Accessibility, SEO, and codebase audit are marked Coming soon.
dimensions.verdict: A Ruttl project is a record of what a person already caught. That's the part Superflow removes.

dimensions.label: How the client says yes
dimensions.framing: Feedback is easy to collect. A yes is harder.
leftFacts: Multi-step review flows: agents check, your team gates, then the client.
Your client opens a link and taps Approve. No account, no login, no app, from their phone.
rightFacts: Guests comment free from a shareable link, no signup.
Approve page locks the page from further comments or edits until unapproved: a real sign-off step.
dimensions.verdict: Ruttl's Approve page is a genuine gate, not just a comment thread. The difference is what happens before it: Superflow's team gates the work first, then the client approves, still no account, from their phone.

dimensions.label: Where you review
dimensions.framing: Half of client work lives behind a password.
leftFacts: Superflow lives on the site itself: passwords, Okta, SSO, no extension needed, guests included.
rightFacts: The live page loads in the project panel. Comment mode is the default.
Edit mode lets you visually change text, images, layout, and HTML and CSS on the live page, a genuine edge.
The Chrome extension covers password-protected sites, login-based apps, and web apps.
dimensions.verdict: Both review the live page. Ruttl's Edit mode goes further than most tools here: real visual and code changes, not just comments. Behind logins, Ruttl needs the extension; Superflow needs none.

dimensions.label: What stays private
dimensions.framing: Your team needs somewhere to disagree.
leftFacts: Internal-only notes your team sees and the client never does.
The debate stays private; the client sees one settled answer.
rightFacts: Private comments are listed on the pricing page as a feature, with per-plan caps.
Whether clients can see them, the internal-only scope: not yet verified.
dimensions.verdict: Ruttl grants the feature; the scope is still open. Renders as a difference only if the client-hidden scope resolves to one.

dimensions.label: What gets captured
dimensions.framing: Both tools pin. The difference is what gets attached without asking.
leftFacts: Element and text pins, area comments.
A screenshot attaches to every comment automatically.
Recordings: screen, video, voice, from the toolbar.
rightFacts: Pixel-pinned comments on the exact element, on live websites, web and mobile apps, images, and PDFs.
Automatic per-comment screenshots: not yet verified. Browser, OS, or screen-size metadata: not yet verified.
dimensions.verdict: Pinning and video comments are even; both are real. Capture is the gap: proof attaches itself in Superflow without a person choosing to record it.

dimensions.label: What it remembers
dimensions.framing: Boards hold tasks. They don't accumulate a client.
leftFacts: Brand rules and past decisions, learned once, fed to the agents next project.
rightFacts: No memory or knowledge concept found. Versioning keeps old versions with their comments, which is not the same as remembering a client.
dimensions.verdict: The tenth project should not start like the first.

dimensions.label: How it fits your stack
dimensions.framing: The fix still has to ship.
leftFacts: Two-way Asana, Monday, ClickUp. Slack built in.
rightFacts: Built-in Kanban workflow. Convert comments to tasks, assign owners, set priority and deadlines.
Integrations: Slack, Trello, Asana, and Jira from the free plan, ClickUp on Pro and up, plus Zapier.
Native two-way sync with a PM tool: not yet verified.
dimensions.verdict: Ruttl's Kanban is built in and its integration list runs deep. If native two-way sync with your PM tool is your spine, weigh that honestly.

scorecard.label: What it costs
scorecard.leftCell: Free / $18 per user per month / Custom (July 2026)

pricingCompetitor: Verified July 2026: Basic Free, 1 project, 5 pages, 10 comments, 1GB storage. The vendor's own pages disagree on users and guests for this plan: the plan card lists up to 5 users and unlimited guests, the comparison table lists 1 user and up to 5 guests. Pro is $18 per month per user, up to 50 users, unlimited projects and pages, 50GB storage, all integrations. Business is custom, with SAML support. Enterprise is custom, with a custom domain and brand colors. Guests are free. No page-view caps advertised.
switchingLines: One snippet on any site; one click on Webflow, WordPress, or GTM.
Paste the checklist you already have; agents assemble from it.
Open Ruttl projects finish in Ruttl. Nothing migrates on day one.
honestCloseStrengths: Ruttl earned its place. Edit mode lets you change text, images, layout, and HTML and CSS on the live page, without touching code. Pixel-pinned comments land on live websites, web and mobile apps, images, and PDFs. Guests comment free from a link, no signup. The Kanban is built in. The Approve page gives you a real sign-off gate, and screen-recorded video comments are part of the toolkit.
stayLine: If pixel-pinned commenting plus live-page visual edits on websites, with free guest links and a built-in Kanban, is what your studio needs, Ruttl is a fine tool. Stay.

faq.question: Is Superflow just Ruttl with AI on top?
faq.answer: No. Ruttl files what a person found; Superflow's agents do the finding. A person makes every call.

faq.question: Do the agents replace my reviewers?
faq.answer: No. Agents run the first pass. Your team, then your client, signs off.

faq.question: What happens to our Ruttl projects?
faq.answer: Finish them in Ruttl. Start new work in Superflow. Nothing migrates on day one.

faq.question: Will our clients have to learn a new tool?
faq.answer: No. They get a link and an Approve button. No account, no login, no app, from their phone.

faq.question: We use Ruttl's Edit mode to change text and layout right on the live page.
faq.answer: Superflow doesn't edit the page. It pins findings for your team to fix and ship. If in-page editing is core to your workflow, weigh that.
